reasoning_trace.value: The paper includes several figures and charts that illustrate the system model, waveform design, and performance metrics of the proposed MU-RO-ISAC system. Figure 1 shows the system block diagram, Figure 2 illustrates the OFDM-MLS-CIM waveform, and Figure 3 depicts the superposed OFDM-MLS-CIM waveforms with different VPP allocation ratios. Additionally, there are several charts that present the BER performance, cross-correlation results, and ranging RMSE of the system.

reasoning_trace.description: Explain the System Mechanism and ISAC Coupling Mode found.
reasoning_trace.value: The proposed MU-RO-ISAC system uses a novel OFDM-MLS-CIM waveform to support both communication and sensing for multiple users. The system mechanism involves OFDM-MLS-CIM modulation, where the input bits of multiple users are modulated into an OFDM signal and an MLS signal, which are then superposed to form the OFDM-MLS-CIM signal. The ISAC coupling mode is based on the superposition of the OFDM and MLS signals, allowing for flexible performance trade-off between communication and sensing.

reasoning_trace.description: Validate the physical consistency of reported metrics (Rate/Resolution).
reasoning_trace.value: The paper reports a data rate of 125 Mbps for OFDM modulation and 7.8 Mbps for CIM modulation, resulting in an overall data rate of 132.8 Mbps for the OFDM-MLS-CIM signal. The ranging resolution is reported to be 6 cm. These metrics are physically consistent with the system parameters and waveform design.

reasoning_trace.description: Identify the solved problems and remaining open challenges.
reasoning_trace.value: The proposed MU-RO-ISAC system solves the problem of supporting multiple users with flexible performance trade-off between communication and sensing. However, the system still faces challenges such as error propagation during IC-aided joint sensing, which needs to be addressed to enhance the sensing performance.
